headline: PayNearMe has launched an AI agent that phones and texts customers about money they owe and also takes their calls to arrange payments.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a practical agent launch in finance, but small and so far backed only by company and pilot-customer claims.
importance_line: People who owe money to lenders and other financial firms may be contacted by an AI rather than a person, and those firms can reach more customers with fewer staff, but the article offers only company and pilot-customer claims, with no independent results.
summary: Finovate reports that the payments company PayNearMe has launched an AI agent that calls and texts customers, answers incoming calls, and helps people make or schedule payments and sort out payment problems, passing them to a human when needed. Indiana Finance Company is piloting it, and its chief operating officer, Carl Stamper, says it gives "the reach of a much larger team", a claim from the pilot customer rather than an independent result.
notes: Launch described as 'this week'; exact day not stated, treated as new today.
